clue.text: Shell found in Jersey ? Right, that's it

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow
that is, written i.e. (id est), the Latin abbreviation

explanation.surface: A beachcomber picks up a shell on Jersey and declares the search over.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, but here it is the cattle breed. The question mark warns that the island is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowrie is a glossy sea snail whose shell was once used as money.

clue.text: Power to hold a Manchester team under cover

indicators.note: under places the following pieces below the cover word, in a down clue

parts.note: a cap is a cover
City is Manchester City, the football club

explanation.surface: A Manchester football side takes shelter as power is held.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity is the ability to contain, the amount something can take in.

clue.text: Sings opening parts of Rule. Britannia in Cambria

indicators.note: in puts those letters inside the country name

parts.note: Cambria is the Latin name for Wales

indicators.note: opening parts of takes the first letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Patriotic song 'Rule, Britannia' is sung in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To warble is to sing with trills, as a songbird does.

clue.text: Putting an obligation on the vicar

definitions.meaning: obligatory, resting as a duty on someone
a holder of a church benefice, such as the parish priest

explanation.definitionFit: Incumbent means binding as a duty, and also the current holder of a church living.

clue.text: Like the secret one unravelled about the inner 8

definitions.text: Like the secret one unravelled about the inner 8

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the next piece
unravelled means the letters of secret plus I are untangled into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
8 refers to the answer at 8 down, a round figure, which is the letter O

explanation.surface: Something mysterious, a secret untangled within an exclusive group.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SECRET and I gives ESTERIC, which goes 'about' O, the ring shape from 8 down. The whole clue also defines: esoteric knowledge belongs to an inner circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is reserved for initiates, a select few on the inside.

clue.text: Mistress mine, can you stand embracing Tiny with two kisses ?

indicators.note: embracing means the word stand goes around the small word

parts.note: taken as written
wee means tiny
a kiss is X, ten in Roman numerals, so two are twenty

explanation.surface: A suitor asks his mistress if she can bear a little one being kissed twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night the song 'O Mistress mine' ends 'Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a term of endearment addressed to the beloved in the Shakespeare song.

clue.text: Old letter North deciphered

indicators.note: deciphered suggests the word North is decoded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An ancient letter from the north is decoded.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn is an Old English runic character for the th sound.

clue.text: If a sailor gets upset, a liqueur's called for

indicators.note: gets upset in a down clue means these words are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: If a seaman knocks it over, someone orders a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratafia is an almond-flavoured liqueur or cordial.

clue.text: Set figure

definitions.meaning: a group of people sharing interests, as in a social group

explanation.definitionFit: A coterie of friends and a round shape share the word.

clue.text: By cutter he hath suffered damage. Peaceful solution

indicators.note: suffered damage suggests the preceding letters have been broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A blade-wielder has caused harm, and a peaceful resolution is sought.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is of BY CUTTER HE HATH.
explanation.definitionFit: To make peace is to put aside a weapon, ending a quarrel.

clue.text: Umbrella protects one in the fall

definitions.text: Umbrella protects one in the fall

parts.words: Umbrella protects one in the fall
parts.note: an umbrella-shaped canopy that keeps someone safe as they drop through the sky, not from rain

explanation.surface: An umbrella keeps someone dry during an autumn shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' suggests autumn (American) or rain falling; the real fall is a drop from an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy of fabric slows a jumper's descent, much as an opened brolly might.

clue.text: Marksman's near miss ?

parts.note: a shot that strikes the target but only its ... ring, close to missing altogether

explanation.definitionFit: On an archery or rifle target the outermost ring, and a shot landing there, carries this name.

clue.text: "Thou shalt not escape ——" Hamlet told Ophelia

definitions.text: "Thou shalt not escape ——" Hamlet told Ophelia

parts.words: "Thou shalt not escape ——" Hamlet told Ophelia
parts.note: a quotation with its final word blanked out: in the nunnery scene Hamlet says that even if Ophelia is chaste as ice she will not avoid slander

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet, Act 3 Scene 1: 'be thou as chaste as ice, as pure as snow' and still the word missing from the quote will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line is 'thou shalt not escape' slander, a false and damaging accusation.

clue.text: Like a bird of the air or vice versa

definitions.text: Like a bird of the air or vice versa

parts.words: Like a bird of the air or vice versa
parts.note: a songbird is full of air in the musical sense, a melody; turn 'full of air' round to air-full and you have the word

explanation.surface: Something resembles a creature of the sky, or the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodious songbird is full of music, and an air is a melody.

clue.text: West End ? East possibly in a sense

indicators.note: End points to the final letter of the word West
possibly signals that the letters of East may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Londoner wonders whether the West End or the East End has more sensibility.
explanation.walkthrough: West End is the London theatre district, but here 'End' takes the last letter of West, T; 'possibly' reworks EAST into ASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, alongside smell and touch.

clue.text: But no disadvantage to the rabbit, of course

definitions.text: But no disadvantage to the rabbit, of course

parts.words: But no disadvantage to the rabbit, of course
parts.note: in golf a rabbit is a weak player, and on the course the strokes allowance helps rather than hinders

explanation.surface: A rabbit on a golf course is not inconvenienced at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbit is golfing slang for a poor player; the allowance of strokes is normally a burden in other sports, but here it helps.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's stroke allowance, usually a word for an impediment, benefits the weaker player.

clue.text: Young devil, 'e's on the ball-what resistance!

parts.note: an imp is a young or little devil
'e is a dropped-h he, giving the letter E
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A mischievous lad on the ball shows great opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedance is electrical resistance in an alternating current circuit.

clue.text: Fleet Street accepts ten unusual donations

indicators.note: accepts means the newspaper word goes around those letters

parts.note: Fleet Street was the London home of the national newspapers, the press

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of ten are reordered

explanation.surface: Newspapers take in ten odd contributions.
explanation.definitionFit: Presents are gifts, things given freely.

clue.text: See Tom about hold-up gossip

indicators.note: about means the word for a tom goes around the delay word

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a hitch is a delay or snag

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to see Tom about a delay, while idle talk goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is light conversation, idle talk about this and that.

clue.text: Pequod's armament put dumb Marxist ahead

parts.note: Harpo was the silent one of the Marx Brothers
on means forward, ahead

explanation.surface: A ship's weaponry puts a silent revolutionary at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pequod is Captain Ahab's whaling ship in Moby-Dick; Marxist means one of the Marx Brothers, not a follower of Karl.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaling ship's weapon is a barbed spear thrown at the whale.

clue.text: This money to burn daily ?

parts.note: banknotes, things set alight in the grate, and a daily ... all share one word

explanation.surface: Someone so rich they can afford to burn money each day.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper money, newspaper put on the fire, and a daily all use the same word.

clue.text: Where this seaside entertainer does his stuff and nonsense

definitions.text: Where this seaside entertainer does his stuff and nonsense

parts.words: Where this seaside entertainer does his stuff
parts.note: a seaside performer works on the jetty
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A seaside performer does his act and talks rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a clown in a white costume who performed in seaside troupes.

clue.text: Flower of the theatre precious to a lady

annotationWithheld.why: Flower of the theatre precious to a lady (6), answer STREAM: 'Flower' is a river, but no parse of 'of the theatre precious to a lady' gives STREAM, and a search found no explanation
annotationWithheld.clue: Flower of the theatre precious to a lady

clue.text: Floosie allowed to be a maid of honour?

parts.note: a tart is a disreputable woman
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A loose woman is permitted to attend the bride.
explanation.walkthrough: A maid of honour is not a bridesmaid here but a small custard tart, a traditional English pastry from Richmond.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid of honour is a small sweet pastry, a kind of little tart.

clue.text: Henry King's around-—the composer

indicators.note: around means the king's name goes outside the letter

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry the king surrounds himself with a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Non-stop description of three blind mice

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off their tails, so they are without ends

explanation.definitionFit: Having no end means ceaseless, and tailless mice lack their rear ends.

clue.text: Hope returns round about the start of an era

indicators.note: round means the turned word goes about the next piece
returns means the word Hope is read backwards

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Optimism comes back as a new era begins.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is the moment that begins a new period of history.

clue.text: Success with series of such raids

definitions.text: Success with series of such raids

parts.note: a hit is a success
and means with, together
a run is a series, as in a run of wins

explanation.surface: A string of successful lightning attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a raid that strikes successfully and then flees.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a raid strikes quickly then withdraws before any response.

clue.text: In which infants are outnumbered?

parts.note: infants in law are those under age, and a smaller group is outnumbered; both senses share one word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both being legally under age and the smaller group.

clue.text: Place about 100 back, to be sure

indicators.note: back means the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: to set is to place
re means about, concerning
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Someone puts something about a hundred yards back, to be certain.
explanation.walkthrough: SET, RE and C run backwards give the old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Certes is an archaic word for certainly.
